audit_findings.title: Reported maintenance capex excludes eventual fleet replacement
audit_findings.mechanism: Understates normalized sustaining capex deducted from owner earnings and therefore overstates the anchor, forecast cash flows and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: Maintenance capital expenditures do not include expenditures to replace compression units when they reach the end of their useful lives.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates that the $76.0 million of 2025 maintenance capex excludes end-of-life unit replacement. That omission matters because the valuation capitalizes owner earnings indefinitely, while gross compression equipment was $4,391.9 million and 2025 depreciation was $259.2 million. The record does not quantify the annualized replacement requirement, but it could materially reduce the $357.8 million anchor and the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Build a unit-level sustaining-capex schedule covering scheduled overhauls, end-of-life replacements and recurring portions of other capex; rerun every scenario with the resulting normalized annual deduction.

audit_findings.title: Post-FY2025 DPS economics are mismatched with the valuation claim
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified net; filed consideration was $726.354 million, including $587.3 million cash and 2.401278 million shares, with those shares equal to 2.31% of the 104.069793 million valuation denominator
audit_findings.mechanism: Mixes a pre-DPS owner-earnings anchor with post-close shares, cash and debt; omits DPS earnings and related recurring financing costs from equity-level owner earnings.
audit_findings.evidence: Per the terms of the purchase agreement, the purchase price includes $575.0 million in cash, subject to adjustment in accordance with the purchase agreement, and the issuance of 2,401,278 shares, representing approximately $100.0 million of the Company’s common stock based on the volume weighted average price of the Company’s stock price for the five days prior to February 5, 2026 of $41.64 to the sellers.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated perimeter error: DPS closed April 1, 2026, so FY2025 contained no DPS operations and was not a partial DPS year. The post-close denominator dilutes the pre-close numerator and omitted DPS earnings understate value, while omitted acquisition-related interest overstates equity owner earnings. The net direction cannot be determined from the supplied valuation, but the bull value of $58.32 is only $4.27 below the $62.59 market price, so the mismatch is reasonably capable of changing the conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Prepare a post-close pro forma anchor using DPS operating results, allocated overhead, taxes, normalized sustaining capex and recurring acquisition financing interest; reconcile all consideration and offering shares to the 104.069793 million denominator and rerun all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: Large sales-tax claim may survive any one-off normalization
audit_findings.magnitude: $65.8 million remained at June 30, 2026; a full bridge deduction would equal approximately $0.63 per share and 1.27% of the $5,165 million base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: Any economic cost added back to owner earnings but still unpaid must reduce the equity bridge or remain as an owner-earnings expense.
audit_findings.evidence: As of December 31, 2025 and 2024, the Company accrued a total amount of $102.3 million and $70.1 million, respectively, relating solely to the Texas portion of the sales and use tax.
audit_findings.explanation: The claim is real, and the latest filing shows that only certain periods were settled and paid: the associated liability declined from $102.3 million to $65.8 million. If none of the remaining amount were already retained in owner earnings, deducting all $65.8 million would reduce base value from $49.63 to about $49.00 per share. That does not change the conclusion relative to the $62.59 price or $34.74 buy-below threshold. Any recurring future sales-tax effect is not established by the record.
audit_findings.action: Trace the settlement payment and remaining $65.8 million by principal, interest, penalties and capitalized amounts; confirm every related OE adjustment, then apply a bridge deduction only for economic cost neither expensed nor deducted through capex.

audit_findings.title: FY2025 anchor includes earnings from the disposed Mexico business
audit_findings.mechanism: Retains disposed-business operating cash flows in the owner-earnings anchor and potentially adds back the separate disposal loss, thereby mismatching the forecast perimeter.
audit_findings.evidence: The majority of the operations were included in the Contract Services segment through the date of sale.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates that Mexico remained in Contract Services through its September 30, 2025 sale, while the valuation forecasts a business that no longer owns it. The filed $33.349 million disposal loss does not quantify Mexico's recurring owner earnings. Without its revenue, operating costs, taxes, sustaining capex and working-capital contribution, the record cannot establish either materiality or direction; removing a profitable operation lowers value, while removing a loss-making operation raises it.
audit_findings.action: Carve the Mexico operation out of FY2025 revenue, cash operating costs, taxes, maintenance capex and working capital; separately reconcile the $33.349 million disposal-loss adjustment and sale proceeds, then rerun the anchor.

audit_findings.title: Long-dated uncommenced leases are absent from the anchor year
audit_findings.magnitude: $47.4 million of filed lease obligations; one commenced lease has a $3.0 million annual base payment, equal to 0.84% of the $357.8 million anchor before tax and approximately $0.29 per share of base value after tax using the model's computed PV multiple
audit_findings.mechanism: The 2025 anchor omits recurring lease expense that begins after the anchor year and therefore slightly overstates forecast owner earnings.
audit_findings.evidence: As of December 31, 2025, we entered into two additional operating leases that has not yet commenced for building and land with lease obligations of $47.4 million.
audit_findings.explanation: The cost was absent from FY2025, but one identified lease commenced June 1, 2026 and is now demonstrable rather than merely hypothetical. Its $3.0 million annual payment is small relative to the anchor; even without assuming replacement of existing costs, its computed base-value effect is about 0.6%. The supplied amounts are not large enough to change the valuation conclusion, although the second lease still requires reconciliation.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the second lease's commencement date and annual payment, determine whether either lease replaces existing facilities, and include only the net incremental after-tax recurring expense in the forecast.

audit_findings.title: OpCo conversion shares may not match the common-only numerator
audit_findings.magnitude: 2025 NCI income was $1.067 million, or 0.30% of the $357.8 million anchor; 0.224 million OpCo-linked preferred shares at June 30, 2026 equal 0.22% of the 104.069793 million denominator
audit_findings.mechanism: An if-converted denominator includes the OpCo economic units while a common-only owner-earnings numerator excludes the earnings attributable to those units.
audit_findings.evidence: Each OpCo Unit is redeemable at the option of the holder for (i) one share of common stock (along with cancellation of a corresponding share of preferred stock) or (ii) cash at Kodiak Services’ election subject to certain conditions.
audit_findings.explanation: The mismatch is demonstrated but conservative and small. Adding the filed $1.067 million of 2025 NCI earnings to the numerator would increase base value by only about $0.14 per share using the valuation's computed operating-PV multiple, while the current linked units are only about 0.22% of the denominator. Neither scale can change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the fully diluted denominator to common shares, OpCo Units, RSUs and PSUs; if OpCo Units remain included on an if-converted basis, add their corresponding recurring earnings and distributions to owner earnings.
